grade.cert.afterSave: The engine derives it after saving.
grade.cert.engine: (computed by the engine from the steps — a suggestion; confirm it when recording)
grade.cert.engineDiffers: the engine computes '{cert}' from the steps — check, or justify the global judgement (GRADE-09)
grade.cert.humanHelp: The final certainty is your judgement (GRADE-09): the level the engine computed from the steps is only a pre-fill — confirm or change it; this goes into the log, and the engine checks that it fits the steps.
grade.cert.noEngine: (this engine version does not derive certainty)
grade.cert.title: Certainty of the evidence
grade.concern: The engine advice signals a downgrade — explain why you do not downgrade.
grade.domains.caption: Downgrading domains — every judgement needs a rationale
grade.fixErrors: Fix the marked fields (every judgement needs a rationale).
grade.gate.noEngine: the engine's GRADE store is unavailable
grade.help.dose_response.asks: Does the effect increase with dose / exposure?
grade.help.dose_response.because: A dose–response gradient strengthens a causal interpretation.
grade.help.dose_response.change: It counts only if it was actually measured and analysed in the studies.
grade.help.imprecision.asks: Is the confidence interval narrow enough for a clear decision?
grade.help.imprecision.because: If the CI crosses no effect or the minimal important difference (MID), or there are few events (below the optimal information size), the estimate is imprecise.
grade.help.imprecision.change: Enter the MID if known: the engine compares the CI with it.
grade.help.inconsistency.asks: Do studies show effects of similar direction and size?
grade.help.inconsistency.because: With large unexplained heterogeneity (high I², wide prediction interval, studies in opposite directions) it is uncertain what to expect in a new setting.
grade.help.inconsistency.change: If a prespecified subgroup explains the differences, or all studies lead to the same conclusion, no downgrade is needed.
grade.help.indirectness.asks: Do the studies' population, intervention, comparator and outcome match your question (PICO)?
grade.help.indirectness.because: If measured in other patients, at other doses or with a surrogate outcome, the result applies only indirectly.
grade.help.indirectness.change: Only a human can judge this: the engine gives no suggestion, but the protocol's PICO helps.
grade.help.large_effect.asks: Is the effect very large (e.g. RR > 2 or < 0.5 in observational studies)?
grade.help.large_effect.because: A large effect is hard to explain by confounding alone, so it can increase confidence.
grade.help.large_effect.change: Only upgrade if there is no serious risk of bias and the effect is consistent.
grade.help.opposing_confounding.asks: Would all plausible confounding work AGAINST the observed effect?
grade.help.opposing_confounding.because: If confounders would reduce the effect yet an effect is seen, the true effect may be even larger.
grade.help.opposing_confounding.change: Rarely applicable; name the specific confounder in the rationale.
grade.help.publication_bias.asks: Is the absence of unpublished (mostly negative) studies likely to bias the result?
grade.help.publication_bias.because: Small-study asymmetry (funnel, Egger/Harbord/Peters, Doi) may suggest it, but with k < 10 the tests are unreliable.
grade.help.publication_bias.change: With a 'suspected' judgement you must decide whether the step is 0 or −1, with a rationale — until then GRADE cannot be recorded (decision 11/4).
grade.help.risk_of_bias.asks: How trustworthy are the included studies (randomisation, blinding, attrition, selective reporting)?
grade.help.risk_of_bias.because: If much of the weight comes from high risk-of-bias studies, the pooled effect may be biased too.
grade.help.risk_of_bias.change: If leaving out the high-risk studies (sensitivity run) does not change the conclusion, downgrading is less justified.
grade.intro: GRADE rates how much we can trust the pooled result. The engine gives evidence and a suggestion per domain (suggestion only); you make the judgement — always with a rationale. The engine derives the certainty from the steps.
grade.journalNone: No GRADE judgement has been recorded for this outcome yet.
grade.leaveBody: Your GRADE or SoF changes are not saved. Leave the screen?
grade.mid.help: As in the protocol (e.g. 0.75–1.25 for RR); the engine parses it and compares the CI with it.
grade.mid.label: MID — minimal important difference (optional)
grade.noOutcomes: No outcomes yet: add one on the Protocol tab.
grade.noRun: This outcome has no committed run yet. GRADE can only refer to a committed run: Analysis tab → Commit.
grade.oldRun: The saved judgement refers to an earlier run. Review the domains with the new run's numbers; saving links the judgement to the new run.
grade.stale: The run is STALE: the data table changed since the run. Re-run the analysis before recording GRADE.
grade.title: GRADE — {name}
grade.upgrades.caption: Upgrading (mainly for observational studies) — a rationale is required when ticked
grade.why.asks: How likely is the true effect to be close to the pooled estimate? We start high for randomised trials and low for observational studies, downgrade for five reasons and may upgrade for three.
grade.why.because: Readers (and guideline panels) need not only the number but also how much to trust it; GRADE gives this through transparent, rule-based steps.
grade.why.change: Give a short rationale for every domain; if you depart from the engine's advice, say why. Do not leave uncertain cases (e.g. suspected publication bias) undecided.
grade.why.title: What is GRADE?
grade.x019.body: With a 'suspected' judgement decide whether the step is 0 or −1, and give a reason. Until then GRADE cannot be recorded; from stage S13 this is an error (X019).
grade.x019.title: Unresolved publication bias.
protocol.class.downgrade: A lower class weakens the privacy rules, so it is recorded as a decision in the project journal.
protocol.class.implicit: The class is not yet recorded in ma-projekt.json; choose it explicitly.
protocol.class.intro: The project's data class decides where the workbench may write and what may go into exports.
protocol.intro: The protocol records WHAT the review asks and what you planned IN ADVANCE. It goes into ma-projekt.json (written by the server, checked by the engine); AMSTAR 2 and the protocol-deviation check (X016) build on it.
protocol.leaveBody: Your protocol changes are not saved. Leave the screen?
protocol.noJson: There is no ma-projekt.json yet: the first save creates it.
protocol.oc.name: Name
protocol.outcome.criticalHelp: GRADE: critical / important / not important; the SoF shows the critical outcomes.
protocol.outcomes.intro: One outcome = one pooled result with its own data table. Critical outcomes come first in the SoF table and in GRADE.
protocol.outcomes.title: Outcomes
protocol.pico.I.help: E.g. GLP-1 receptor agonist before conception.
protocol.pico.O.help: E.g. major congenital malformation; give the time point too.
protocol.pico.P.help: E.g. women planning pregnancy with type 2 diabetes.
protocol.question.intro: Briefly state who, which intervention, compared with what, and which outcome the review is about.
protocol.question.title: Research question (PICO)
protocol.reg.idHelp: Exactly as given by the registry (e.g. CRD420241234567).
protocol.reg.intro: A preregistered protocol is the critical AMSTAR 2 item 2: give the registry and the identifier (e.g. PROSPERO CRD42…).
protocol.reg.title: Registration
protocol.sp.name: Spec
protocol.spec.needRef: Prespecified only with a protocol reference.
protocol.specs.empty: No analysis plan (spec) yet: create it on the Analysis tab.
protocol.specs.intro: Mark as prespecified the analysis plans that are in the registered protocol, with a reference (e.g. 'protocol 9.2'). Do not mark post-hoc analyses this way: if the primary analysis differs from the prespecified one, it is a protocol deviation that must be logged as a decision (X016).
protocol.specs.title: Prespecified analyses
protocol.type.diagnostic.help: Sensitivity and specificity of a test (QUADAS-2).
protocol.type.intervention.help: Randomised or non-randomised studies of a treatment effect (RoB 2, ROBINS-I).
protocol.type.label: Type
protocol.type.prediction_model.help: Performance of prediction models (PROBAST+AI, TRIPOD+AI); the risk-of-bias tab switches accordingly.
protocol.type.prognostic_factor.help: Association of a factor with a later outcome (QUIPS).
protocol.type.title: Review type
protocol.why.asks: PICO is the four parts of the question: Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome.
protocol.why.because: It drives the search, eligibility and the GRADE indirectness domain; AMSTAR 2 item 1 asks for it too.
protocol.why.change: Changing it during the review is a protocol deviation: record it as a decision in the Log.
sof.caption: Summary of Findings
sof.captionNote: — every cell is engine text; the source field is in the cell tooltip
sof.export.help: Exports the saved table into 06_kezirat/sof/. The CSV is Excel-safe: text cells that look like formulas get a ' prefix.
sof.intro: Every number in the table is computed by the engine from the committed run (relative effect, participants, absolute effect per assumed risk); certainty comes from the GRADE judgement. Here you only set the assumed risks and your own footnotes.
sof.noRun: The SoF needs a committed run (Analysis → Commit).
sof.note.label: Footnote {n}
sof.oldRun: the saved table is from an older run — save again
sof.risk.label: Label / source
sof.risk.noCite: without a source the footnote will read 'source: not given' — add the citation (GRADE 12)
sof.risks.help: The absolute effect depends on the assumed risk. The default is the pooled control-arm risk; if a clinically more relevant one exists (e.g. a national registry), add it as external, with its source.
sof.title: Summary of Findings (SoF)
